text:
The app currently contains 26 investigation summaries returned by its PSI combustion query and 21 numeric rows from the PSI-22 table, per the repository snapshot in this project. These counts describe the loaded snapshot, not all PSI content. The app labels source gaps instead of replacing them with synthetic experimental measurements.

Primary data: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI), combustion investigation query: https://psi.nasa.gov/physci/repo/search?q=combustion&data_source=psi&data_type=investigation

name: title-3
text: Compare oxygen conditions without conflating them

name: subtitle-3
text: Three separate quantities: oxygen concentration, total pressure and calculated oxygen partial pressure.

name: moon-insight
text: Moon example: 30% is 42.9% above Earth’s 21% oxygen concentration. At 10.2 psi total pressure, calculated ppO₂ is 3.06 psi—close to Earth’s 3.09 psi. Concentration alone is not a fire-risk score.

These are reference scenarios from the challenge text, not PSI experimental measurements. The Moon example shows the exact boundary values requested: 30% O2 and 10.2 psi total pressure; 0.30 × 10.2 = 3.06 psi ppO2. Earth calculation: 0.21 × 14.7 = 3.087 psi, rounded to 3.09. Spacesuit: 1.00 × 4.3 = 4.3 psi. Challenge text describes Moon-base concentration as more than 40% higher than Earth's; (30−21)/21 = 42.9%, a concentration-only comparison. The “30% or greater” and “10.2 psi or less” ranges do not imply a unique partial pressure without a selected pair of values. Do not infer risk from oxygen concentration alone.

Challenge source: https://www.spaceappschallenge.org/2026/challenges/flame-in-freefall/

name: evidence-vs-inference

alt: NovaForge investigation explorer screenshot with searchable investigation records

text:
Family groupings and investigation names are shown to help orient users; the PSI query snapshot and linked records remain the authority for details. ACME includes six gaseous-flame experiments; CFI-G investigates high-oxygen microgravity combustion conditions (up to 85% O2 per the challenge description). E-FIELD applies electric fields to flame-generated ions; it is not a partial-gravity test. The dashboard keeps evidence score and inferred relevance score separate. Any unavailable conditions remain unavailable.

text:
The SI assistant is retrieval-augmented: it retrieves relevant loaded dataset records before generating an answer, cites investigations/records, and should report when the dataset does not support an answer. In no-key configuration, the interface uses DEMO (cached) mode; do not describe it as live AI. The app's TESTING.md documents available and unavailable questions.

name: title-7
text: Know what the snapshot cannot answer

name: subtitle-7
text: Clear gaps are part of a trustworthy safety-research tool.

name: gap-text-0
text: O₂ concentration, pressure, ppO₂ and airflow are missing from many loaded summaries.

name: gap-text-1
text: This PSI query snapshot does not include LUCI or FM² partial-gravity records.

name: gap-text-2
text: NASA separately reports LUCI simulated lunar-g testing; FM² studies materials at lunar 1/6 g.

name: gap-text-3
text: E-FIELD Flames uses electric fields on flame ions; it does not simulate partial gravity.

name: disclaimer
text: Educational research tool · Not a certified safety system · NASA is not affiliated with or endorsing NovaForge

In this specific PSI combustion query snapshot, many summaries do not expose oxygen concentration, total pressure, calculated ppO2, or airflow values; use individual linked records to check availability. This snapshot excludes LUCI and FM2. Do not repeat the challenge prompt's older premise as a current global claim that NASA has no partial-gravity combustion data: NASA has reported LUCI simulated lunar-gravity combustion tests separately. NASA describes FM2 as studying burning materials on the Moon at one-sixth Earth gravity. E-FIELD Flames applies electric fields to flame-generated ions; it is not gravity manipulation. Microgravity and normal gravity results may bound intermediate gravity but do not directly establish outcomes.
